national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu today said that the textile and apparel sector is not only an important part of India’s cultural heritage but also provides livelihood to millions of people. Addressing the convocation ceremony of the National Institute of Fashion Technology (NIFT), the President called upon students to adopt a global outlook while remaining rooted in the country’s rich cultural heritage and values. Emphasising the growing role of women in the fashion industry, the President said around 85% of the nearly 4000 students present at the event are women. She said India has immense potential to expand its global presence in fashion and textile technology. The President urged students to use their knowledge, skills and creativity to connect the country’s traditional textile heritage with contemporary markets and new technologies. Calling upon the youth to contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047, the President said students should not remain merely job seekers but should strive to become job providers and create employment opportunities for others. President Murmu said that over the past four decades, NIFT students and professionals have made significant achievements at the national and international levels, bringing recognition to India. She appreciated the contribution of NIFT professionals in promoting Indian textiles, silk and design traditions on the global stage. President Murmu congratulated the graduating students, their parents and award winners for outstanding academic performance. Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh said, in 2008, then President Dr A P J Abdul Kalam delivered the NIFT convocation address, and after 18 years, again President Droupadi Murmu blessed the students. He said around four thousand students today received their degrees. Textiles Secretary and Chairperson of the Board of Governors, NIFT, Neelam Shami Rao said the students are graduating at an exciting time for textiles, fashion and design. She said the industry they will enter is changing at a remarkable pace, and the boundaries between craft, fashion, design, engineering, creativity, technology and textiles are becoming increasingly fluid. The Secretary said the fashion of tomorrow can draw strengths from the craft traditions of India.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | National 51 Government notifies Semicon 2.0 scheme with 1.27 lakh crore rupees outlay
national_raw_news.content: The government today notified the Semicon 2.0 scheme with an outlay of Rs 1.27 lakh crore to boost the chip manufacturing ecosystem in the country. With this, India could account for nearly 10 percent of the global semiconductor industry market in the coming years and is expected to play a much bigger role in the global semiconductor value chain, Union Minister for Electronics and Information Technology Ashwini Vaishnaw said while addressing a press briefing in New Delhi today. Mr. Vaishnaw added that the focus of the Government is towards making the country firmly embedded in the global semiconductor value chain, from wafer fabrication to chip production. After releasing the notifications for all six pillars of the Semicon India Programme 2.0., Mr Vaishnaw noted that there is confidence among global semiconductor industry stakeholders that India is the right destination for major investments in the coming decades. The Minister underlined that the speed at which projects have moved from approval to ground-breaking and then to commercial production in Semicon 1.0, has been particularly noted by the industry. Further, Mr. Vaishnaw said India’s talent pool, policy certainty and ease of working have contributed to the industry’s growing interest in making India a base for semiconductor manufacturing and design. He added the country’s objective is to become an indispensable part of the global semiconductor supply chain, with global industries increasingly depending on India for production and design. Mr Vaishnaw emphasised that developing the entire ecosystem in the country will be foundational for sustained growth of India’s semiconductor industry over the next 50 years.

national_raw_news.title: 2 hours ago | International 201 Death toll in Nepal flash flood rises to 903, while more than 4,247 people still missing
national_raw_news.content: In Nepal, the death toll from last week’s devastating floods and mudslides has risen to 903, while more than 4,247 people remain untraceable. According to the Nepal’s National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, the figure has increased from Sunday’s figure of 2,502. Bodies have been recovered from all eight affected districts of Nepal as rescuers race against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded. Meanwhile, at least 933 workers are believed to be trapped at around half a dozen hydropower projects. Rescue teams backed by India and other experts are searching around half a dozen blocked hydropower tunnels, including Trishuli-3A. In Tibet, the death toll currently stands at 16, with 546 reported to be missing. The disaster sent a torrent of ice, rock, mud and debris through towns and villages along the Nepal-Tibet border. An Indian tunnel rescue team is working with the Nepali Army at hydropower sites in Chilime and Langtang. Earth-moving machinery and soldiers have been working through the night to clear debris. Nepali Army spokesperson Raja Ram Basnet said the massive deposits are making tunnel access difficult. A preliminary study by Nepali scientists found the floods were triggered by a massive ice-rock avalanche at around 5,200 metres in Rasuwa’s Langtang-Lirung area. The debris entered the Lhende River before surging through the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli. Nepali Prime Minister Balendra Shah called the floods an “unprecedented and devastating natural disaster”, with nearly 21,000 security personnel involved in rescue operations. The Red Cross estimates more than 90,000 people were affected, while authorities continue recovering and identifying bodies.

national_raw_news.title: 8 hours ago | International 334 PM Modi arrives in Bishkek on two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan; to attend SCO Summit and meet several ...
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has arrived in Bishkek on a two-day visit to Kyrgyzstan. He was received at the airport by Kasymaliev Adylbek Aleshovich, chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers. A traditional Kyrgyz dance performance was also organised to welcome him. Mr Modi is visiting Kyrgyzstan at the invitation of President Sadyr Zhaparov for 26th SCO Summit. On the first day of his visit to Kyrgyzstan, PM Modi will hold bilateral meetings with SCO leaders on the sidelines of the summit. He will also participate in several other programmes. Mr Modi will address the SCO Summit tomorrow. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will first interact with the Friends of India in Bishkek today. He will then visit the Mahatma Gandhi Memorial Park and pay floral tributes at the statue of Mahatma Gandhi. The statue was unveiled by Mr Modi during his visit to Kyrgyzstan in the year 2015. The Prime Minister will also hold bilateral meetings with several leaders of SCO member countries today. These include meetings with the Presidents of Armenia, Kyrgyzstan and Iran, as well as a bilateral meeting with the President of Russia. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games today. The event celebrates the rich and vibrant cultural heritage of Central Asia. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will address the 26th Summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation tomorrow, the first of September. Vikalp Shukla, Akashvani News, Bishkek.” In his departure statement on Saturday, Mr Modi said he is looking forward to advancing India’s vision for the region, based on “security, connectivity and opportunity”. He also said India will work with SCO members towards a region free from “terrorism, separatism and extremism”. Mr Modi will also attend the opening ceremony of the 6th World Nomad Games. He said the visit will strengthen India’s strategic partnerships in Central Asia, deepen its civilisational connect with the region and advance the shared pursuit of peace, stability and prosperity. The summit theme is “25 Years of the SCO: Together Towards Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity. The summit’s priorities include counter-terrorism, regional stability and coordination on cross-border threats. The Bishkek Declaration and other summit texts are expected to be finalised during heads-of-state session tomorrow.

national_raw_news.title: Gujarat to host 11th Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit in January next year 2 hours ago 40
national_raw_news.content: The 11th Vibrant Gujarat Global Summit 2027 will take place from 10th to 12th January next year in Gandhinagar. The theme of this summit is Viksit Gujrat – Shaping Global future. Addressing a curtain-raiser press conference in New Delhi today, Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendrabhai Patel said it is Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s vision that Gujarat should not merely be seen as an investment destination but should emerge as a growth engine for the country. He said the State government has realised this vision on the ground and is working to make Gujarat the soft power of the country. Mr Patel added that the government is promoting green hydrogen and green energy and has introduced sector-specific, holistic policies to promote ease of doing business. Referring to the ‘Saptdhara’, or seven streams of development, announced by Prime Minister Narendra Modi from the ramparts of the Red Fort during his Independence Day speech, Mr. Patel said it covers key sectors including agriculture, food processing, technology and innovation. He said these sectors will receive further impetus through the Vibrant Gujarat Summit. On the occasion, Union Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports Dr. Mansukh Mandaviya said that Gujarat has transformed itself in line with future requirements and has emerged as one of the country’s leading investment destinations. He said Gujarat has developed a strong investment ecosystem, supported by close linkages between entrepreneurs and investors. Dr. Mandaviya said, Gujarat offers opportunities across various sectors and described the semiconductor industry as a sunrise sector with significant growth potential. The Vibrant Gujarat summit has evolved as one of the most reputed global forums for business networking, knowledge sharing and strategic partnerships for inclusive growth and sustainable development. The Vibrant Gujarat initiative was conceptualised in 2003 under the leadership of Narendra Modi, then Chief Minister of Gujarat. Over the years, the summit has expanded from an investment-focused event into a broad platform connecting governments, multinational corporations, investors, entrepreneurs, policymakers, academics and innovators. The Vibrant Gujarat model is designed to connect overseas governments and companies with Gujarat’s industrial ecosystem.

national_raw_news.title: BJP State Working Committee meeting enters second day in Orchha, Madhya Pradesh 2 hours ago 41
national_raw_news.content: The second day of the BJP State Working Committee meeting is being held today in Orchha, Madhya Pradesh. During the meeting, Chief Minister Dr. Mohan Yadav visited the Ram Raja Temple this morning and offered prayers. After the visit, the Chief Minister reviewed the development work going on at Ram Raja Lok. He spoke about preserving the historical buildings and promoting Orchha’s traditional style of architecture. On the second day of the meeting, a special workshop is being held under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan. The workshop will finalise the upcoming programmes related to public service, good governance and strengthening the party organisation. Several senior BJP leaders attended the first day of the meeting. State BJP President Hemant Khandelwal said that service, values and the welfare of the last person are the foundation of the BJP’s ideology. State in-charge Dr. Mahendra Singh stressed the need to strengthen the organisation at the booth level to achieve the goal of making India a developed nation by 2047. Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan spoke about taking farmer welfare schemes to the people. Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia linked the growing use of UPI, startups and technology with new opportunities for young people. Deputy Chief Minister Rajendra Shukla said that the Ken-Betwa project is important for the development of the Bundelkhand region. The meeting also discussed issues related to women’s empowerment, tribal communities and employment.
